previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson, a right-handed male with mixed Hodgkin's and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma involving the central nervous system and eyes, was admitted for his tenth maintenance cycle of high-dose methotrexate and second dose of rituximab. He was pre-medicated with dexamethasone and Benadryl prior to rituximab to prevent infusion reactions and received IV fluids and sodium bicarbonate during methotrexate infusion to protect his kidneys. He developed transient transaminitis, which improved with increased leucovorin and hydration. Methotrexate levels declined appropriately, and a follow-up MRI showed no new lesions or evidence of lymphoma recurrence. He was discharged home in stable condition on a prednisone taper, three days of leucovorin, and sodium bicarbonate, with instructions to monitor for concerning symptoms and attend follow-up appointments.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ man with a history of mixed 
Hodgkin's and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma with CNS and ocular 
involvement who presents for methotrexate and rituximab.

(1) CNS Lymphoma:  He received methotrexate at a dose of 6 g/m2 
and rituximab.  This was followed by leucovorin rescue.  He was 
also given hydration with alkaline fluids, bicarbonate standing 
and PRN to maintain urine pH in the basic range,  anti-emetics 
PRN.  Methotrexate levels were monitored.  Level was 0.13 uM on 
the day prior to discharge.  MRI brain showed no recurrence.  

(2) Renal Tuberculosis:  Resolved after treatment.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Previously known CNS lymphoma.

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made to numerous previous MR studies of the head
extending from ___ to ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Sagittal T1, axial FLAIR, T2, T1, gradient echo images were
acquired through the brain.  Following administration of intravenous
gadolinium, axial T1 and sagittal and gradient echo images were obtained
through the brain.  Coronal and axial reformatted gradient echo images as well
as diffusion-weighted images were also reviewed.

FINDINGS:
Overall, the study is unchanged from that done in ___.  Again seen is
a small FLAIR hyperintense focus in the left frontal lobe (4:23) with
associated hypodensity on gradient echo images, likely related to old retained
blood products or calcification.  Otherwise, there is no abnormal focus of
contrast enhancement.  Scattered punctate FLAIR hyperintensities are
nonspecific, though unchanged and likely the sequela of chronic microvascular
infarction. There is no vascular territorial infarction, edema, mass effect.
The ventricles and sulci are normal in size and caliber.

IMPRESSION:
No evidence of lymphomatous recurrence and no change since ___.
